hints: Write down where a single cell `(row, column)` has to end up after the turn. Is there a pair of simpler operations that together do the same thing?
A clockwise quarter turn is a reflection in the main diagonal followed by a reflection left-to-right. Each of those is easy to do in place.
Transposing swaps `grid[r][c]` with `grid[c][r]` - and only for `c > r`, or every swap is undone by its twin.
Reversing each row afterwards is the left-to-right reflection, and it is a two-pointer walk per row.
